clue.text: Bolted after the horse — it's too late!

definitions.text: Bolted after the horse — it's too late!

parts.words: Bolted after the horse — it's too late!
parts.note: the saying about shutting the barn's entrance only once the animal has already run off, read as a definition

explanation.surface: A rueful cry on finding a horse has run off before anyone fastened anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the proverb about shutting this only after the horse has bolted; 'Bolted' looks like the horse's flight but is also what is done to the door.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names the barn entrance that is locked uselessly once the animal has escaped.

clue.text: Time that is right for a row

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone says the timing is just right for a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one level or rank in a series, a row as of seats.

clue.text: It may take an age to get a suntan

definitions.meaning: a prehistoric period named after the metal
the brownish colour skin gains in the sun

explanation.surface: A slow sunbather complains it takes forever to brown.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal names a prehistoric era, and its colour describes tanned skin.

clue.text: Dissolute vice got Edward expelled

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, so the letters of the word beside it are loosened and rearranged

parts.note: Ted is a familiar short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A debauched character called Edward is thrown out for his vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissolute' is the anagram signal on 'vice', giving EVIC; 'got' is only a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be evicted is to be turned out of a property, put out or expelled.

clue.text: Start work in French -at this university?

parts.note: op., short for opus, is a musical work
en is the French word for 'in'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you begin your studies in French at a particular university.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'at this university?' is an extra nod to the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university, rather than part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something is to begin or start it, as a shop opens for business.

clue.text: Dazed US general overturned and encircled

annotationWithheld.why: Dazed US general overturned and encircled (7): REELING is R(EEL)ING, LEE reversed inside RING, but 'encircled' must give RING and signal the container at once, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Dazed US general overturned and encircled

clue.text: Two boys with a collection of 19th century objects

parts.note: Victor is a boy's name
Ian is a second boy's name

explanation.surface: Two lads and someone else gather up old Victorian bric-a-brac.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana means objects and artefacts from the reign of Queen Victoria, the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Joint accompaniment?

parts.note: a joint here is a roast of meat, and the question is what is served alongside it at Sunday lunch

explanation.surface: Something that goes along with a shared effort or a smoked cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a shared venture or a body part; it is a joint of roast meat, served with greens and roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrots, peas and potatoes are the side dishes that accompany a roast.

clue.text: One of the main dangers in war

definitions.text: One of the main dangers in war

parts.words: One of the main dangers in war
parts.note: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open sea, so the danger is an explosive device floating in it

explanation.surface: A list of the chief perils of warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' reads as 'chief' but is the sea, so the danger is a naval explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval mine is an explosive device laid in the sea to sink ships.

clue.text: The old bone-shaker is strangely-loved piece

indicators.note: strangely says the following letters are to be set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone is oddly fond of a rattling antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges LOVED PIECE; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bicycle with iron tyres was nicknamed a bone-shaker for its rough ride.

clue.text: Very much the opposite

parts.note: the reverse of 'much' in the sense of quantity; 'very' added both ways keeps the phrases matched

explanation.surface: An emphatic contradiction of what was just said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very much the opposite' reads as an emphatic denial; take it as 'the opposite of very much', i.e. very small in amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The antonym of a large amount is a small amount.

clue.text: Guided a horse holding half the rein

indicators.note: holding means the horse word keeps the next letters inside it

parts.note: a steed is a horse

indicators.note: half the means only the first two of the four letters of rein are used

explanation.surface: A rider steered a horse while gripping only half the rein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the' signals taking the first two letters of 'rein'; 'holding' is the container signal, and 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to direct a course, so a vehicle that was steered was guided.

clue.text: Uncast replacements?

parts.note: roles in a play that have no actor yet are 'uncast', and a phrase for spare components also describes them

explanation.surface: A question about substitutes who were never chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for replacement components is read as roles (parts) left over (spare) after casting.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare components are kept to replace broken ones; here also theatrical roles left unfilled.

clue.text: Simple way in which the affluent live

parts.note: simple means easy
a street is a way, a road

explanation.surface: An observation that the rich live an uncomplicated life.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on this road is an idiom for living in comfort and wealth.

clue.text: Bob from Sandy Lane

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A man called Bob comes from a road named Sandy Lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters from inside 'Sandy Lane'; Bob is the singer Bob Dylan.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is the American singer-songwriter, so his first name stands for his surname.

clue.text: A country road ran crookedly

indicators.note: crookedly means bent out of line, so the letters of the two words before it are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rural road twisted its way along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A country' looks like an adjective for the road but is the definition; 'crookedly' rearranges ROAD RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small Pyrenean principality between France and Spain.

clue.text: A spirited harp-player?

parts.note: 'spirited' reads as lively but means being a spirit, and heavenly beings are pictured with harps

explanation.surface: A lively musician on the harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirited' suggests a lively performer; it means a spirit, the harp-playing being of heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly messengers are traditionally pictured playing harps in the clouds.

clue.text: Coming to a vital conclusion

parts.note: 'vital' means to do with life, so the conclusion reached is the end of life

explanation.surface: Arriving at a crucial decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital' looks like 'crucial', but it means 'of life', so this is a life coming to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at death's door has a life that is ending.

clue.text: Primate embraces son in church recess

indicators.note: embraces means the first word wraps round the next one

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A primate hugs a boy inside a church alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, apt for a church, but it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the vaulted semicircular end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Not a square dance, presumably?

parts.note: the formal dance shares its name with a round object, so it cannot be square

explanation.surface: A guess that some event is not a country-style square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A formal dance shares its name with a round object, so it is presumably not square.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal social dance is called by the same word as a sphere.

clue.text: As a cricketer, Edward is restrained

parts.note: a cricketer at the crease is a bat, a batsman
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward is restrained in his cricket play.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is often simply called a bat; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Held in, as in 'with breath held', meaning reduced or restrained.

clue.text: Risk taking a chance about meat on the bone?

indicators.note: about means the wager word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken, a wager

explanation.surface: Gambling on whether some meat is still attached to the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, wrapping the wager round 'Risk'; 'taking' is only a link. The question mark admits the meat is often, not always, on the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the breast, often sold with the bone in.

clue.text: Ma is upset after Dad discovers the art of anarchy

indicators.note: after says the rearranged piece comes behind the father's word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: upset means overturned and disordered, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mum is distressed when Dad discovers anarchic art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges 'Ma is' (giving AISM) and 'after' places that behind the father; 'discovers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The early twentieth-century anti-art movement mocked convention in a deliberately anarchic way.

clue.text: Sort of sea bird from China?

parts.note: the East Sea is one named sea, the compass point serving as a type
the erne is a sea eagle, a bird

explanation.surface: A kind of seabird that comes from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea bird' reads as one phrase but splits: the sea is a sort named for a compass point, and the bird is the sea eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the Orient, so things from there are oriental.

clue.text: They're not often miscast in Westerns

definitions.text: They're not often miscast in Westerns

parts.words: They're not often miscast in Westerns
parts.note: 'miscast' seems to be about actors' roles, but these ropes are cast, thrown, by cowboys

explanation.surface: Remarks on how rarely the parts in cowboy films are badly cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miscast' points to film casting; these ropes are cast, thrown, by cowboys, who seldom miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassos with running nooses used by cowboys for catching cattle.

clue.text: Eye disease -girl catches it

indicators.note: catches means the name grabs the next piece and holds it inside

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl comes down with an eye infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' is the container signal: the girl's name holds 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflammation of the coloured part of the eye.

clue.text: Gunners return to the lines with weapons

indicators.note: return means the letters of the gunners' abbreviation are sent back the other way

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British army
rows are lines

explanation.surface: Artillerymen go back to their positions with their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns RA into AR; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Missiles shot from a bow are traditional weapons.

clue.text: Dining room offers hash

definitions.meaning: the room where military personnel eat together
a hash is a muddle or botched job

explanation.surface: A canteen serves up a dish of chopped meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces' eating hall; also a botch or jumble.

clue.text: A small number turned up at church on one occasion

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Only a few people came to church just the one time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives ON from NO; 'A' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Means a single time, on one particular occasion.

clue.text: What a quartet must do to avoid discord?

definitions.text: What a quartet must do to avoid discord?

parts.words: What a quartet must do to avoid discord?
parts.note: discord read musically as clashing notes, which four singers prevent by staying on pitch

explanation.surface: Advice to four people on keeping the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discord' suggests quarrels; read musically it is clashing notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing or playing on the correct pitch prevents a musical clash.

clue.text: It's a lot older than you

definitions.text: It's a lot older than you

parts.words: It's a lot older than you
parts.note: an archaic form of the pronoun 'you', older as a word than the modern one

explanation.surface: Someone is told something is far more ancient than they are.
explanation.walkthrough: It seems to say something has more years than the reader; it means an older form of the word 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic second-person singular object pronoun, used before 'you' replaced it.

clue.text: Slave-driver teacher after a job

indicators.note: after places the teacher word behind the job word

parts.note: a task is a job
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: A harsh overseer is a teacher looking for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding boss who pushes people hard, metaphorically a driver of slaves.
